title: Dark Mode Design System
summary: This lesson covers essential principles for creating a professional dark mode UI, moving beyond simple black and white. It teaches techniques for depth, elevation, text legibility, and handling accents and images.

transcript.text: Black background. White text.
That's not dark mode. That's a terminal.
Near black, not black.
Pure black saves OLED battery. It also kills depth.
Nothing sits lower than black, so every surface fights for one plane.
Start near black. Now your layers have room.
Lightness is elevation. Shadows die on dark.
Black on black is invisible. So your card floats nowhere.
Raise it with lightness. The higher the surface, the lighter it gets.
Three tiers of white. Pure white text vibrates.
Full contrast on a dark surface burns after one paragraph.
Drop it to 87%. Secondary at 60. Disabled at 38.
Three tiers, one variable.
Calm the accent. Your brand blue bleeds.
Saturated color on a dark surface glows past its edges and outshines your content.
Lighten it. Desaturate it. Same hue, less weight.
Alpha hairlines. Edges need a hairline.
One pixel of white at 8% alpha reads on any surface.
Use alpha, not a fixed gray. The line adapts as the surface lightens.
Dim the photos. Photos glare on dark.
A bright image on a dim page pulls every eye.
Dim it to 90% brightness.
Illustrations get a dark variant, not a filter.
Dark mode is a system.

design_principles: Use near-black instead of pure black for depth
Avoid pure white text to reduce eye strain
Use alpha transparency for text hierarchy
Dim images and redraw illustrations for dark mode
before_after: A flat, high-contrast black and white dashboard is transformed into a layered, accessible, and visually balanced dark mode interface.
